note: The original description is Emerson 1925, Anoplotermes (Speculitermes) arboreus, based only on a single queen (no soldier; this genus has no soldiers either); the genus Ruptitermes was separated off later. The text was extracted by OCR from a library scan on the Internet Archive.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (The type specimen is a queen.) Head dark brown, oval, covered with fairly short hairs and longer setae. Fontanelle concolorous with the head, large and round, similar to that of A. silvestrii. Antenna: segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3, segment 3 equal to segment 4. Compound eyes medium-sized, not close to the lower margin of the head; ocelli fairly large, projecting, about their own width from the compound eye. Postclypeus dark brown, the median line indistinct or absent. Pronotum dark brown, the lateral margins rounded, the posterior margin slightly concave. Meso- and metanotum with white margins on both sides, the posterior margin narrow and deeply concave. Coxae and femora dark brown; fore tibia mostly dark, the rest yellow; mid and hind tibiae mostly yellow, the tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites dark brown. Measurements: head length 1.83 mm; head width 1.67 mm; compound eye diameter 0.43 mm; pronotum length 0.90 mm, width 1.61 mm; hind tibia length 2.30 mm; queen body length 19 mm, abdominal width 4.80 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: It differs from A. reconditus (Silvestri 1903, small oval fontanelle) and from the form recorded by Holmgren 1906 (slit-like fontanelle); Emerson considered that the latter two may each be a distinct species. This species is the only member of the genus in British Guiana that nests several feet or more above the ground; the worker head is dark and distinguishes it from the other species of the genus in British Guiana. Type locality: Kartabo, British Guiana, the only locality known; the type specimen is a queen. The description is based on a single queen collected by the author at Kartabo, where the species is evidently scarce, only 3 colonies being seen, and the nest differs clearly from the other nests nearby.
